scope: A human-facing, non-canonical organization of the frozen Liu research record. Canonical evidence remains at its historical path and in mainlines/liu_v1.

canonical_path_policy.rule: Keep frozen historical files at their registered paths; organize them through physical study capsules. New research may be born inside a capsule once its runner and contract use that path natively.
canonical_path_policy.scientific_authority: mainlines/liu_v1/manifest.json and the historical registered contracts and result files
canonical_path_policy.catalog_role: Organize scientific questions, findings, negative constraints, provenance files, and reading routes without creating a new estimand.
canonical_path_policy.migration_boundary: Relocating a frozen canonical file requires a separately versioned provenance migration with compatibility mapping and full replay validation; it is not a navigation edit.

migration_audit.decision: Use physical study capsules now, pin frozen historical paths, and allow new studies to be capsule-native from inception.

status_legend.frozen_mainline: Frozen reporting-level synthesis; changes require an erratum or a new mainline version.
status_legend.frozen_contract: Task or evaluation boundary used by later studies; not itself a mechanism result.
status_legend.confirmed: Positive result supported by the registered controls in its stated seed scope.
status_legend.supporting: Valid evidence used to localize or constrain a mechanism, without closing the full question.
status_legend.mixed: Contains important positive evidence and a registered failure or unresolved primary link.
status_legend.valid_negative: Competence-qualified negative that rejects or closes the registered candidate family.
status_legend.unresolved: The registered test did not identify a unique or sufficient explanation.
status_legend.transported: The registered mechanism transported across the stated one-factor boundary.
status_legend.historical: Development or qualification evidence retained for provenance, not the current headline result.
status_legend.deferred: Prospectively prepared work that is outside the current model-focused program.
status_legend.context: Source or background material; not a node in the model evidence chain.

views.purpose: The shortest route for a talk or manuscript: task, competence, final causal mechanism, algorithmic asymmetry, and transport boundary.

views.purpose: How the project moved from a competent global-only model to the P_T/a_T mechanism while preserving valid negative results.

views.purpose: Valid negative routes that should not be reopened without contradictory evidence or a separately frozen scientific question.

studies.title: Liu Mainline v1 frozen evidence overlay
studies.question: Which historical results jointly support the reportable Liu v1 model claim?
studies.finding: A frozen claim DAG, artifact bundle, replay contract, and four-figure report view bind the reportable evidence without replacing historical experiments.
studies.boundary: This catalog is only a human locator around Liu Mainline v1; it cannot change the frozen manifest, report view, hashes, artifacts, or scientific assertions.

studies.title: Liu task and human benchmark contract
studies.question: What information and response boundary must every model-facing Liu analysis preserve?
studies.finding: The task contract preserves item identity, signed displayed magnitude, passive four-presentation learning, all-pair testing, and no test feedback.
studies.boundary: Classic rewarded adjacent-pair TI and list linking are context, not descriptions of the Liu observation interface.

studies.title: Development and qualification record
studies.question: Did the initial candidate satisfy enough competence and causal gates to justify formal study?
studies.finding: The early candidate established development evidence and qualification infrastructure that motivated the frozen pilot and formal contracts.
studies.boundary: Single-seed development output is provenance, not formal multi-seed confirmation or the current headline model.

studies.title: Pilot and formal behavioral confirmation
studies.question: Does the global-only v1 mechanism jointly reproduce the registered Liu behavioral conjunction across unfiltered seeds?
studies.finding: All ten formal networks remained competent and preserved major causal and geometric positives, but every network failed the full behavioral conjunction with a shared excessive-distance-slope and learned-accuracy fingerprint.
studies.boundary: The common negative motivates a missing direct-local mechanism; it does not erase global reassembly or authorize seed filtering, temperature tuning, or checkpoint selection.

studies.title: Frozen v2.4 behavioral reproduction map
studies.question: Which Liu behavioral phenomena are quantitatively reproduced and which remain mismatched by the final frozen model?
studies.finding: Six of nine registered phenomena are reproduced and three are qualitatively reproduced but quantitatively mismatched; none is absent.
studies.boundary: This is a competence and phenomenology map, not evidence that humans use the same internal mechanism or that the fit is complete.

studies.title: Assembly slope and Hodge diagnostics
studies.question: Does stable evidence omission explain the excessive symbolic-distance slope?
studies.finding: The slope mismatch localizes to the neural policy transformation: neural fields are almost additive while human choices retain a stronger learned-pair residual.
studies.boundary: This is a policy-level mixed-code signal, not proof of a local memory store.

studies.title: Prefix and relation-LOO assembly trajectory
studies.question: How does retained evidence causally shape remote relations and the terminal global field?
studies.finding: Retained support trials immediately affect remote pairs, leave relation-specific LOO signatures, and converge toward an expected-rank-like terminal potential rather than a hard MAP order.
studies.boundary: Remote absolute effects are robust, but independent correctness-propagating Bayesian updates are not established.

studies.title: Support-write localization
studies.question: Which factors determine the content, gain, and sensitivity of an episode-local fast-weight write?
studies.finding: Eligibility carries evidence-specific direction, modeled DA has a coarser gain role, and alpha places actual writes in high-gain recurrent directions.
studies.boundary: Modeled DA is not identified with Bayesian surprise, and alpha placement is not a unique posterior-direction map.

studies.title: Causal support factor swap
studies.question: Are eligibility direction and DA-linked magnitude causally transferable factors of support writing?
studies.finding: Matched eligibility transfers donor relation direction, DA changes downstream magnitude, and actual alpha placement beats norm-matched permutation controls.
studies.boundary: One formal seed later showed DA-direction heterogeneity, so direction preservation is not a universal implementation invariant.

studies.title: History state-by-factor closure
studies.question: Does assimilation arise from generated write factors, the accumulated recurrent state, or their matched interaction?
studies.finding: Accumulated P has a reproducible positive effect on local recurrent expression with a smaller positive history-matched interaction; the total factor-generation main effect remains unresolved.
studies.boundary: Assimilation cannot be assigned solely to eligibility, DA, or a scalar learning rate.

studies.title: Formal mechanism confirmation
studies.question: Does the registered global fast-weight mechanism replicate across ten unfiltered formal networks?
studies.finding: Six of seven primary mechanism links confirm, including global reassembly, direction transfer, sensitivity placement, history effects, and expected-rank-over-MAP projection; the DA direction-preservation threshold fails through seed-2009 heterogeneity.
studies.boundary: The complete seven-link chain is not confirmed, and seed 2009 cannot be filtered or used to erase the six replicated links.

studies.title: Hidden learned-relation residual audit
studies.question: Is an existing cross-relation correctness direction present in response hidden state but suppressed by W_out?
studies.finding: A small direct-enriched residual exists, but no shared correctness direction is hidden from the current readout; the simplest readout-only route is rejected.
studies.boundary: The result does not show that persistent local information is absent at earlier operator states.

studies.title: Relation-trace localization
studies.question: Where does relation identity appear between generated writes, terminal fast weights, and query dynamics?
studies.finding: Registered static prototype geometry fails in write and terminal matrices, but relation identity appears at the first fast-weight-sensitive query transition and persists after response.
studies.boundary: This is a mixed operator-code result, not a shared static embedding, correctness channel, or proof that persistent information is absent.

studies.title: State-by-query operator binding
studies.question: Does the fast-weight state preserve relation identity through congruent query-dependent operator action?
studies.finding: State-relation identity and exact query matching replicate in preactivation and nonlinear hidden effects, while query-invariant cross-query identity fails.
studies.boundary: The state is a basis-dependent query-addressable operator, not a rank-one key-value memory or an established correctness code.

studies.title: Operator-output semantics
studies.question: At what stage does a correctness-aligned local operator signal become misexpressed?
studies.finding: A and J_b A are correctness-aligned, but exact finite-amplitude tanh degrades the signal and reverses H>A, localizing the missing link to nonlinear expression.
studies.boundary: The result does not license a new readout, activation change, or global scalar gain.

studies.title: Operator amplitude and curvature path
studies.question: How does finite-amplitude nonlinear expression reverse otherwise correct local value?
studies.finding: H>A shows a robust mean zero crossing, F>A crosses in a subset, and correctness-opposed quadratic curvature is relation- and subject-conditioned.
studies.boundary: The pattern is not generic saturation and does not select global clipping or post-hoc adaptive amplitude points.

studies.title: Unsigned curvature gate
studies.question: Can unsigned hidden-space curvature magnitude safely control local response amplitude?
studies.finding: The gate preserves competence and global mechanism but fails aggregate rescue and specificity, harms the other seven relations, and assigns attenuation in the wrong state direction.
studies.boundary: Reject unsigned curvature magnitude as the online control variable; preserved global and operator positives remain supported.

studies.title: Policy-relative curvature-opposition gate
studies.question: Can the instantaneous sign of projected first- and second-order terms select harmful curvature?
studies.finding: All competence gates pass, but critical H>A/F>A states almost never satisfy the opposition condition and the candidate fails rescue and control specificity.
studies.boundary: The sign is informative in controls, but scalar amplitude gating is closed; do not add a third risk statistic or co-adaptation rescue.

studies.title: First-order policy residual
studies.question: Is preserving the existing first-order branch through one low-capacity policy correction sufficient for local fidelity?
studies.finding: The natural residual causally moves H>A and F>A toward correctness with state-query specificity, but aggregate rescue and control specificity fail and six correct relations decline.
studies.boundary: Preserve the causal residual fingerprint, but close low-capacity response-expression correction as a sufficient mechanism.

studies.title: Conjunctive persistent local-trace pilot
studies.question: Can a separately persistent, query-addressed local state preserve direct experience alongside P_T?
studies.finding: The pilot establishes a strong P/L causal double dissociation and direct-enriched local rescue, but its registered sampled learned-accuracy conjunction fails.
studies.boundary: The discovery pilot is not a full behavioral rescue and does not establish unique tensor-product coding or biological stores.

studies.title: Local behavioral non-rescue attribution
studies.question: Why can a large direct-causal local rescue produce only a tiny sampled learned-accuracy change?
studies.finding: Stable-omitted cells dominate learned error mass, retained cells are mostly near ceiling, and the local trace removes retained exact error while sampled accuracy remains endpoint-sensitive.
studies.boundary: The historical 0.65 rule still misses narrowly; the result cannot be relabeled as the original pilot PASS or repaired by increasing gain.

studies.title: Independent local-trace mechanism replication
studies.question: Do local direct rescue, address specificity, and the P/L double dissociation replicate on independent backbones?
studies.finding: All four registered links pass separately on seeds 2102 and 2103 with artifacts jointly locked before Liu evaluation.
studies.boundary: This is replicated mechanism evidence, not a network-population prevalence estimate or a solution to the remaining global-policy mismatch.

studies.title: Differential evidence-access pilot
studies.question: Can broader weak observed evidence enter the unchanged local state while global assembly retains selective admission?
studies.finding: The zero-parameter v2.4 equation rescues omitted direct fidelity with evidence and query specificity while preserving the global/local causal scope.
studies.boundary: A first execution is explicitly noninterpretable; the source-locked repaired result is canonical, and p_sr is not established as the unique human encoding rule.

studies.title: Fresh-backbone differential-access confirmation
studies.question: Does the unchanged v2.4 differential-admission mechanism confirm on fresh independent backbones?
studies.finding: All four links confirm independently on seeds 2104 and 2105, promoting P_T/a_T with differential evidence admission to the working model mechanism.
studies.boundary: Retained probability has a small replicated cross-talk cost, global distance slope remains excessive, and population prevalence is not established.

studies.title: Global-policy slope localization
studies.question: Which algebraic part of the pure-global neural policy carries the excessive nonlearned distance slope?
studies.finding: The positive neural margin slope is already in the additive potential; the Hodge residual and fixed sigmoid are compressive rather than amplifying.
studies.boundary: The later common-unit audit rejects the stronger claim that neural additive norm is globally over-sharp relative to the posterior comparator.

studies.title: Global-policy amplitude provenance
studies.question: Is the neural/posterior slope mismatch explained by excessive total additive amplitude?
studies.finding: Neural additive norm is smaller than the posterior comparator even though neural slope is steeper, converting the issue from scalar calibration to field allocation and shape.
studies.boundary: The outcome is comparator-sensitive and unresolved; temperature, P_T, W_out, and scalar corrections are not licensed.

studies.title: Additive-by-residual field reassembly
studies.question: Does additive source, residual source, or their fixed-sigmoid context close the neural/posterior slope gap?
studies.finding: Additive source and norm-matched shape effects are positive, the fixed-sigmoid interaction is negative, and neither component alone closes the comparator.
studies.boundary: Pre-sigmoid interaction is exactly zero; the probability-space context effect is not a network-internal multiplicative circuit.

studies.title: Fresh-backbone field-fingerprint replication
studies.question: Do the additive-source, equal-energy shape, and fixed-sigmoid interaction fingerprints replicate on new backbones?
studies.finding: A>0, Q_shape>0, and I<0 replicate independently on seeds 2106 and 2107 after joint artifact locking.
studies.boundary: R remains unresolved and cannot be upgraded to equivalence; no single field component is shown sufficient.

studies.title: Equal-energy allocation audit
studies.question: Where does equal-norm neural-versus-posterior additive allocation differ, and which cells exactly carry Q_shape?
studies.finding: The exact delta-g to delta-p to per-pair q bridge localizes a replicated, policy-effective allocation fingerprint.
studies.boundary: The first execution is noninterpretable and preserved as such; comparator-relative localization is not evidence that the neural network incorrectly encodes uncertainty.

studies.title: Exact-posterior comparator adequacy
studies.question: Is the exact-posterior comparator externally adequate on human distance slope and reliable pair structure?
studies.finding: Both registered adequacy criteria fail, so the stable neural-posterior fingerprints remain facts but cannot define a neural intervention target.
studies.boundary: The result rejects the comparator as an external target; it does not invalidate the earlier comparator-relative algebraic identities.

studies.title: Human-only metric constructive comparator
studies.question: Can a task-faithful, metric-preserving constructive comparator generalize from preregistered humans to the held-out replication cohort?
studies.finding: The candidate reproduces held-out human distance slope but fails the reliable distance-residualized pair field and cannot become a neural target.
studies.boundary: Comparator search on the same responses is closed; the first failed execution is noninterpretable, and human-mechanism validation is deferred.

studies.title: Potential-transition reduction v1
studies.question: Can current global potential and evidence close the next potential transition?
studies.finding: The registered rank-two potential-transition reduction is insufficient.
studies.boundary: This rejects the tested reduction, not every nonlinear or trajectory-dependent compact global state.

studies.title: Scalar-history reduction v2
studies.question: Does adding low-capacity scalar history close global update amount?
studies.finding: Scalar history is insufficient, while preserving evidence that update amount depends on history.
studies.boundary: The negative does not deny history dependence; it rejects the registered scalar closure.

studies.title: Item-history reduction v3
studies.question: Does a richer item-history coordinate close global learning dynamics?
studies.finding: The registered item-history state is insufficient, while exposing relational allocation structure that scalar history misses.
studies.boundary: Do not infer irreducible high dimensionality from failure of this registered coordinate family.

studies.title: Functional fast-weight latent sufficiency
studies.question: Does alpha times P contain a stable cross-episode linear coordinate sufficient beyond current potential and evidence?
studies.finding: The full-P oracle fails held-out generalization and worsens prediction in every backbone; the registered linear sufficiency audit is negative.
studies.boundary: This is a readout upper bound, not an autonomous latent rollout or proof that no nonlinear episode-specific coordinate exists.

studies.title: Asymmetric algorithmic organization synthesis
studies.question: What is the simplest algorithmic statement supported by the complete model evidence stack?
studies.finding: The local L_T state has an exact edge-ledger-plus-Gram reduction a_T, while the global output is geometrically near-additive but its tested learning states do not close.
studies.boundary: Simple output geometry does not imply simple learning dynamics, and failed reductions do not prove intrinsic high dimension.

studies.title: Support-topology transport
studies.question: Does the P_T/a_T mechanism survive a one-factor change in the Liu support graph?
studies.finding: The registered structural mechanism transports under the repaired, source-locked topology contract.
studies.boundary: The original attempt is retained as an attempt result; transport across selected graphs is not an arbitrary-graph guarantee.

studies.title: Presentation-order transport
studies.question: Does the mechanism persist when the same physical support trials are reordered?
studies.finding: All registered links transport across random, clustered, and reversed schedules; the local ledger is exactly commutative while P_T remains quantitatively order-sensitive.
studies.boundary: Mechanism transport is not behavioral or P_T invariance.

studies.title: Evidence-sparsity transport
studies.question: Does the functional asymmetry transport across matched connected graphs with seven to ten support relations?
studies.finding: All causal components transport through E=9 and nearly all at E=10, but one stable-error prevalence gate fails; the prediction that denser evidence reduces P_T reliance is rejected.
studies.boundary: The registered outcome remains SPARSITY_DEPENDENT_OR_UNRESOLVED and cannot be relabeled as complete seven-to-ten transport.

studies.title: Sparsity individualization localization
studies.question: Does density regularize global orders generally or create a replicated E=10 family-specific loss of stable errors?
studies.finding: Subjective orders converge and several error measures decline with density, but binary stable-error incidence loss is not replicated and E=10 family contrasts remain unresolved.
studies.boundary: This explains parent heterogeneity without upgrading the sparsity parent outcome.

studies.title: Item-count transport
studies.question: Does the functional asymmetry transport out of distribution to six- and ten-item Liu-style cycles?
studies.finding: All primary links pass at N=6, 8, and 10 across all three development backbones, including exact local ledger reconstruction and P/a double dissociation.
studies.boundary: N covaries with support duration, query count, and direct-query fraction; global policy degrades with size, so this is not arbitrary-size scaling.

studies.title: Magnitude-placement human validation program
studies.question: Which new human manipulation could distinguish task-faithful metric construction theories after comparator search on existing responses failed?
studies.finding: The protocol, randomization, schema, synthetic validation, and collection-readiness records are preserved for a later human experiment.
studies.boundary: No new human data are treated as collected here, and this program is intentionally paused while the project focuses on the model mainline.

studies.title: Source papers and background
studies.question: Which source documents define the experimental and model lineage?
studies.finding: The Liu source paper and background neural-network paper are retained as reading context.
studies.boundary: A source PDF is not a frozen model result, registered contract, or causal evidence node.
